target.title: fix(agents): avoid repeated item progress snapshots
target.body:
## Summary

- Stop re-sending already displayed preamble item text when a later same-item progress snapshot extends text after the prior snapshot has flushed.
- Keep the fix limited to item progress delta calculation, with a focused regression test for the flushed-prefix case.

## What Problem This Solves

ACP child parent-stream relay stores the latest `itemId` preamble snapshot text, but it only sliced prefix updates when the previous snapshot was still pending in the local flush buffer. After the first snapshot flushed to the parent, a later same-item snapshot like `Planning done` still starts with the already displayed `Planning`, so the old code sent the full `Planning done` text and duplicated visible parent-side progress.

## User Impact

Parent sessions receive cleaner child-agent progress updates: once `codex: Planning` has already been displayed, a later same-item snapshot `Planning done` adds only `codex: done` instead of repeating the already shown `Planning` prefix.

## Origin / follow-up

- **Follows / completes:** #95404, which added parent-stream/item progress handling as part of Codex assistant partial streaming.
- **Gap this fills:** #95404 covered snapshot coalescing before a flush, but the same item prefix-update case after a flush still re-sent the full snapshot and duplicated already displayed text.
- **Consistency:** This keeps the existing item snapshot map as the source of truth and applies the same prefix-delta rule regardless of whether the previous snapshot is still buffered or has already flushed.

## Competition / linked PR analysis

- Searched open PRs for `acp-spawn-parent-stream progress snapshot` and `acp-spawn-parent-stream Planning done`; no open PR covered this parent-stream duplicate-after-flush bug.
- #92236 is an open WebChat/native Codex commentary progress PR. It projects native app-server progress into WebChat and does not touch `src/agents/acp-spawn-parent-stream.ts` or the parent relay item snapshot delta calculation.
- This PR is intentionally narrower than broader progress/commentary UI work: it only fixes duplicate parent-session text emitted by the ACP parent relay.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Same `itemId` preamble snapshots should not repeat text that the parent stream relay has already flushed to the parent session.
- **Real environment tested:** Local OpenClaw follow-up worktree on Linux with Node v22.22.0, running the actual `startAcpSpawnParentStreamRelay`, real `emitAgentEvent` bus, and real `drainSystemEventEntries` parent queue path.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** `node --import tsx --input-type=module` started the parent relay with progress commentary enabled, emitted `item/preamble` for `Planning`, waited for flush, drained the parent queue, emitted the same `itemId` snapshot `Planning done`, waited for the second flush, and drained the parent queue again.
- **Evidence after fix:**

```json
{
  "relay": "startAcpSpawnParentStreamRelay",
  "eventBus": "emitAgentEvent",
  "parentQueue": "drainSystemEventEntries",
  "inputEvents": [
    {
      "itemId": "preamble-1",
      "kind": "preamble",
      "progressText": "Planning"
    },
    {
      "itemId": "preamble-1",
      "kind": "preamble",
      "progressText": "Planning done"
    }
  ],
  "observed": {
    "afterFirstFlush": [
      "codex: Planning"
    ],
    "afterSecondFlush": [
      "codex: done"
    ]
  }
}
```

Before the fix, the focused regression test failed because the second parent-side output repeated the already displayed prefix:

```text
Expected: "codex: the app-server stream"
Received: "codex: Checking the app-server stream"
```

Focused regression test after the fix:

```text
pnpm vitest run src/agents/acp-spawn-parent-stream.test.ts
Test Files  2 passed (2)
Tests  72 passed (72)
```

- **Observed result after fix:** The first snapshot flush emits `codex: Planning`; the later same-item prefix snapshot emits only `codex: done`, so the parent side does not repeat text that was already visible.
- **What was not tested:** No third-party channel service was launched; the proof uses the local OpenClaw parent relay, real event bus, and real parent system-event queue because the bug is in local agent parent/child progress delivery, not in an external transport.
- **Fix classification:** Root cause fix

## Maintainer-ready details

- **Maintainer-ready confidence:** High — the diff is a one-line production delta calculation change plus one focused regression assertion, with before failure, after test pass, and local real relay proof.
- **Why it matters / User impact:** Progress text is user-visible in parent sessions; repeated prefixes make child-agent progress noisy and can look like duplicated work or duplicated message delivery.
- **Architecture / source-of-truth check:** The source-of-truth state is `itemProgressTextById`, which records the last full snapshot per item; delta calculation should compare against that state even after the pending flush buffer has been cleared.
- **Patch quality notes:** Patch quality warnings were considered: this is not a fallback or downstream dedupe hack; it fixes the owner calculation at the item snapshot delta boundary and keeps existing replacement behavior for non-prefix snapshot changes.

## Merge risk

- **Risk labels considered:** merge-risk: message-delivery; merge-risk: session-state.
- **Risk explanation:** The touched code controls parent-visible progress delivery and per-item snapshot state, so incorrect behavior could drop or duplicate progress text. The change is constrained to same-item prefix updates; unrelated new text snapshots still emit full text, and same snapshot equality still no-ops.
- **Why acceptable:** The regression test covers the flushed-prefix failure mode, existing tests still cover buffered coalescing and replacement snapshots, and the real relay proof exercises the actual event bus and parent queue path.

## Review findings addressed

N/A — new follow-up PR; no maintainer or reviewer findings exist for this branch yet.

## Regression Test Plan

- **Target test file:** `src/agents/acp-spawn-parent-stream.test.ts`
- **Scenario locked in:** Same `itemId` preamble progress emits `Checking`, flushes, then emits `Checking the app-server stream`; the second parent-side message must contain only the new suffix `the app-server stream`.
- **Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail:** The test uses the existing parent relay harness and real event delivery into the relay, so it locks the exact state transition that caused duplication without adding a broader runtime fixture.
- `pnpm vitest run src/agents/acp-spawn-parent-stream.test.ts`
- `node --import tsx --input-type=module` local relay proof through `startAcpSpawnParentStreamRelay` + `emitAgentEvent` + `drainSystemEventEntries`

## Risk / Compatibility

Low to medium. This is a message-delivery/session-state path, but the behavior only changes same-item prefix snapshots after a prior snapshot was recorded. Non-prefix replacements still send full replacement text, duplicate identical snapshots still no-op, and buffered prefix updates keep the existing compacted output behavior.

## What was not changed

- **What did NOT change:** Only same-item prefix delta calculation changed; event routing, heartbeat wakeups, ACP projection settings, assistant delta handling, non-prefix item replacement behavior, and external channel delivery are unchanged.
- Did not change how item progress is enabled or gated by channel progress commentary settings.
- Did not change assistant stream handling or replaceable assistant snapshot behavior.
- Did not add transport-specific dedupe logic.

## Root Cause

- **Root cause:** `appendItemProgressSnapshot` tracked the previous full text per `itemId`, but it only sliced a prefix update when that prior text was still pending in the flush buffer. Once `flushPending` cleared the buffer, the same prefix relationship still existed in `itemProgressTextById`, but the relay ignored it and emitted the full later snapshot.
- **Why this is root-cause fix:** Prefix delta calculation now uses the recorded per-item snapshot as the invariant, independent of pending-buffer state, so already displayed text is not re-sent after flush while non-prefix snapshot changes still replace appropriately.
